bulwark.loop: Build Guard through actually blocked attacks; spend it on timed mitigation or a counterstrike. Face the next physical hit rather than holding one passive stance indefinitely.
bulwark.route_a: Mobile interception: preserve frontal defense while advancing and use Interpose to protect an ally who cannot move.
bulwark.route_b: Static defense: hold a small area, pool Guard and answer a predictable tank strike with a stronger personal response.
bulwark.tradeoff: Mobile protection loses some stationary mitigation; stationary specialization loses rescue reach. Neither removes baseline tanking.
bulwark.resource_contract: 100 Guard; +10 on a real block or effective interception, once per second; 25 for a defensive spend; lose 10/second after six seconds out of combat.

armsmaster.loop: Create up to three Openings with deliberate attacks; consume them on a high-value target while using parry windows selectively.
armsmaster.route_a: Precision dueling: remain close, build Openings and delay the finisher for an exposed target.
armsmaster.route_b: Reach and control: spend Openings on line pressure and movement disruption while switching targets.
armsmaster.tradeoff: Focused timing raises priority-target output but reduces multi-target coverage; reach gives up peak single-target pressure.
armsmaster.resource_contract: Three Openings per caster on the current target; primary generator adds one; spender uses one to three; eight-second duration, refreshed only by eligible hits.

berserker.loop: Build Frenzy with connected weapon sequences, then decide between spending it on an area attack and sustaining a risky offensive window.
berserker.route_a: Controlled aggression: smaller incoming-damage penalty and defensive recovery at high Frenzy.
berserker.route_b: Pursuit aggression: chain short legal repositions and spend Frenzy during multi-target pressure.
berserker.tradeoff: Safer offense sacrifices peak burst; pursuit needs uptime and takes more damage when careless.
berserker.resource_contract: Five Frenzy; one per eligible weapon action, at most once per second; area spender consumes three; lose one every two seconds after four seconds without a hit.

oathkeeper.loop: Generate Oathmarks through real protection and spend them on threat or mitigation; place defensive zones where the group can actually use them.
oathkeeper.route_a: Area protection: stay within a compact Vigil Circle and plan damage-reduction windows.
oathkeeper.route_b: Moving protection: redirect capped damage and move protection between allies instead of defending one location.
oathkeeper.tradeoff: Large area efficiency declines when the party moves; mobile rescue reduces personal stationary mitigation.
oathkeeper.resource_contract: Five Oathmarks; one for an eligible block/prevention event, once per second; spend two; no marks from standing idle in a zone.

crusader.loop: Build Conviction and target Seals with weapon actions, then consume Seals on a prepared finisher.
crusader.route_a: Single-target verdict: maintain one marked opponent and concentrate resource spending.
crusader.route_b: Sweeping judgment: spread marks through a cone and divide a spender across several opponents.
crusader.tradeoff: Target focus loses cleave; spreading loses priority-target peak damage and takes setup.
crusader.resource_contract: 100 Conviction shared with class; +10 eligible generator; three target Seals maximum; finisher spends 30 Conviction and available Seals.

justicar.loop: Alternate targeted recovery with optional close-range holy attacks; reserve Testament for expensive recovery windows.
justicar.route_a: Melee-assisted healing: earn Testament from safe weapon contact between heals.
justicar.route_b: Ranged protection: remain with vulnerable allies and build through effective healing instead.
justicar.tradeoff: Melee contribution risks positional exposure; ranged play gives up martial damage and accelerated resource generation.
justicar.resource_contract: Five Testament; one from an effective primary heal or eligible attack while an ally is injured, once per second; spend three on group recovery. Mana sustains healing.

high_priest.loop: Use inexpensive direct healing for routine damage, preserve Devotion for group recovery and keep emergency healing available.
high_priest.route_a: Efficient recovery: use varied small heals and time the larger prayer for predictable group damage.
high_priest.route_b: Emergency recovery: hold resources and a burst heal for a threatened target, accepting higher mana use.
high_priest.tradeoff: Efficient preparation has less instant recovery; emergency specialization is less sustainable.
high_priest.resource_contract: Five Devotion; one per effective heal of a different ability family from the previous qualifying heal; spend three on group healing; Mana remains the primary budget.

oracle.loop: Place wards before damage and earn Foresight only when they prevent real damage; spend it on the next predicted danger.
oracle.route_a: Concentrated forecasting: protect one marked recipient with larger timed wards.
oracle.route_b: Distributed forecasting: divide protection among several allies before an area pulse.
oracle.tradeoff: Single-target wards waste value when damage changes targets; distributed wards are weaker on a tank spike.
oracle.resource_contract: Five Foresight; one per consumed shield event above 1% recipient maximum health, once per second; spend three; no resource for unused or refreshed wards.

inquisitor.loop: Apply evidence marks through sacred attacks, then choose when to consume them for a verdict.
inquisitor.route_a: Sustained testimony: keep marks active and use measured single-target casts.
inquisitor.route_b: Area testimony: use a witness field and consume marks on clustered opponents.
inquisitor.tradeoff: Sustained damage has slower burst; area specialization loses efficiency on isolated enemies.
inquisitor.resource_contract: Three evidence marks per caster/target; primary direct hit adds one; finisher consumes all; 12-second expiry.

pyromancer.loop: Build Heat while applying Burning; decide between consuming Heat now and preserving setup for a later detonation.
pyromancer.route_a: Ignition burst: consume Heat and selected Burning on one priority target; reapply the burn afterward.
pyromancer.route_b: Sustained combustion: preserve Burning and spend Heat on limited spreading/area pressure.
pyromancer.tradeoff: Detonation creates stronger short windows but downtime afterward; sustained play needs targets to live and remain reachable.
pyromancer.resource_contract: 100 Heat; Kindling Spear +10, Flash Ember +5 on valid hits; ordinary spender costs 30; major finisher consumes available Heat above 30; no gain from consumed remaining DoT damage.

frostbinder.loop: Apply Chill, then choose between consuming it for damage and maintaining space with slows and areas.
frostbinder.route_a: Focused shatter: consume Chill frequently for direct damage against a priority target.
frostbinder.route_b: Zone control: retain Chill pressure and invest in larger, weaker control fields.
frostbinder.tradeoff: Shatter loses persistent control; zoning loses immediate single-target output. Bosses receive the authored damage alternative instead of roots.
frostbinder.resource_contract: Five Chill per caster/target; primary frost hit adds one, at most once per action; finisher consumes three; ten-second expiry; root follows global diminishing returns.

arcanist.loop: Build Arcane Charges with Glyph Bolt and trade burst against rapidly increasing mana cost when spending charges.
arcanist.route_a: Charged burst: accumulate four charges, then release Charge Lance from a prepared position.
arcanist.route_b: Efficient circulation: spend one or two charges, recover mana between windows and favor limited mobile follow-ups.
arcanist.tradeoff: Maximum charges improve burst but consume mana disproportionately; frequent smaller spends reduce peak output.
arcanist.resource_contract: Four Arcane Charges; Glyph Bolt +1; Charge Lance consumes selected 1–4 charges; damage 0.8P +0.35P per charge, mana cost 3% +2% per charge; charges expire after ten seconds out of combat.

gravecaller.loop: Allocate one summon-capacity pool and command coordinated attacks; resources come from successful combat, not dismiss/resummon loops.
gravecaller.route_a: Single sovereign: one elite controlled servant, fewer commands and concentrated target pressure.
gravecaller.route_b: March of bones: up to four lesser servants with divided output and coordinated positional coverage.
gravecaller.tradeoff: Elite control is vulnerable to disabling one pet; a squad costs more attention and has weaker individuals, not four full pet budgets.
gravecaller.resource_contract: Four capacity units; elite costs four, lesser costs one; all sources share the same aggregate pet budget. Commands cost 20 Soul Essence; basic owner attacks generate 10, once per action.

plaguebringer.loop: Maintain diseases, collect bounded Contagion from actual ticks and choose between extending, spreading and consuming them.
plaguebringer.route_a: Patient decay: longer diseases with preserved total-per-application budgeting and lower maintenance frequency.
plaguebringer.route_b: Rapid infection: shorter diseases and faster damage realization at greater mana and refresh pressure.
plaguebringer.tradeoff: Long effects lose value on short-lived targets; rapid infection is more demanding and easier to exhaust.
plaguebringer.resource_contract: 100 Contagion; +5 from a qualifying disease tick, global owner limit once per second; spread costs 25; acceleration costs 30; harvest consumes the selected target's remaining disease budget once.

soulreaper.loop: Mark one enemy, build Essence through direct and channel attacks, then choose a spender or defensive reserve.
soulreaper.route_a: Repeated extraction: smaller frequent spends and controlled life drain.
soulreaper.route_b: Planned requiem: pool Essence for a telegraphed finisher while retaining enough for a ward.
soulreaper.tradeoff: Frequent spending loses burst; pooling risks interruption and reduces immediate self-protection.
soulreaper.resource_contract: 100 Soul Essence shared with class; marked direct hit +10, channel tick +5; ordinary spender 30; major spender 60; no resources from self-damage or friendly summons.

minstrel.loop: Maintain up to two ordinary song slots, heal targets actively and spend Harmony on group recovery without requiring precise audio timing.
minstrel.route_a: Moving chorus: move with allies, use short restorative phrases and frequent song transitions.
minstrel.route_b: Prepared haven: establish longer recovery patterns and hold an emergency finale.
minstrel.tradeoff: Mobile healing trades peak sustained throughput; prepared healing loses value when allies scatter.
minstrel.resource_contract: Three Harmonies; +1 on an effective primary heal, at most once per second; group recovery consumes two and finale three. Mana is primary; Cadence is the performance meter.

skald.loop: Generate Cadence in melee, then choose personal finishing damage or a temporary group enhancement.
skald.route_a: Solo skald: more personal weapon output and reduced allied amplification.
skald.route_b: Battle chorus: spend more time and Cadence on measurable ally enhancement.
skald.tradeoff: Personal damage scales less with coordinated allies; group support performs poorly when allies cannot act. Neither route requires another player to complete solo content.
skald.resource_contract: 100 Cadence; Iron Verse +10 on contact; War Chant upkeep four/second, Thunderbeat cost 25, finisher 40; strongest-category group buff only.

virtuoso.loop: Build a short sequence of offensive note families, then resolve it into a bounded sonic effect.
virtuoso.route_a: Focused solo: narrow line attacks and direct single-target final notes.
virtuoso.route_b: Echo control: use a field and disruptive notes to support clustered combat.
virtuoso.tradeoff: Narrow attacks lose coverage; echo fields need positioning and cannot recursively repeat their own damage.
virtuoso.resource_contract: Store the last three qualifying note-family IDs; repeated identical notes do not advance the sequence; resolving a finale clears it; maximum one weakened echo per original attack.

assassin.loop: Prepare a poison/positioning window and spend Combo Points on a timed finisher rather than attacking from stealth indefinitely.
assassin.route_a: Poison attrition: maintain poison, accept slower damage and use defensive re-entry windows.
assassin.route_b: Opening burst: commit positional attacks and finish during a short marked weakness.
assassin.tradeoff: Poison pressure is slower; burst is weaker when forced out of position or its opening is denied.
assassin.resource_contract: Five Combo Points on the owner, not a target; eligible generator +1; finisher spends 1–5. Stealth itself grants no points and cannot be retoggled in combat to farm an opener.

duelist.loop: Alternate attacks with counters to build Advantage; spend it only when the exchange creates an opportunity.
duelist.route_a: Counter specialist: read incoming attacks and turn a successful parry into a finisher.
duelist.route_b: Mobile exchanges: build through varied weapon actions and short positional changes.
duelist.tradeoff: Counter play loses value without incoming eligible attacks; mobile play gives up the strongest counter reward.
duelist.resource_contract: Five Advantage; +2 from a successful active parry or +1 from two distinct qualifying attacks, once per second; finisher consumes three; no gain from self-created attacks.

saboteur.loop: Place a small device set, control an approach and trigger it deliberately rather than spawning unrestricted traps.
saboteur.route_a: Prepared field: deploy fewer stronger devices and wait for enemies to enter the planned area.
saboteur.route_b: Mobile sabotage: use shorter-lived devices and reposition between activations.
saboteur.tradeoff: Prepared damage is avoidable by moving away; mobile devices have lower individual impact.
saboteur.resource_contract: Three active devices, separate from cosmetic objects but within the class combat-object ceiling; placement cost 20 Energy, trigger cost 10; each device triggers once.

marksman.loop: Build Aim while stationary and consume it on measured shots; movement is permitted but has an explicit opportunity cost.
marksman.route_a: Anchored marksman: hold position for stronger deliberate shots and planned narrow volleys.
marksman.route_b: Mobile precision: preserve a limited amount of Aim through brief repositioning at reduced stationary bonuses.
marksman.tradeoff: Anchoring is vulnerable to hazards and melee pressure; mobility sacrifices peak stationary damage.
marksman.resource_contract: Three Aim; gain one per uninterrupted second preparing an attack, maximum three; moving removes one per second unless a talent permits limited retention; no random accuracy bonus.

beastmaster.loop: Build Bond with successful owner/pet coordination and spend it on commands, while retaining functional owner attacks.
beastmaster.route_a: Offensive bond: pet and owner focus one priority target with timed combined attacks.
beastmaster.route_b: Guarding bond: use more commands for pet interception and protection while reducing direct pet offense.
beastmaster.tradeoff: Offense loses defensive command availability; guarding loses damage and cannot replace a player tank.
beastmaster.resource_contract: 100 Bond; +10 when both owner and pet hit an eligible target within two seconds, once per two seconds; command costs 25; one active four-capacity companion.

pathfinder.loop: Combine a ranged attack, a close-range technique and traps with legal repositioning; select safe routes rather than permanent kiting immunity.
pathfinder.route_a: Ambush route: plan traps and use short melee pressure when the target reaches them.
pathfinder.route_b: Running route: prioritize mobile shots and defensive waypoints.
pathfinder.tradeoff: Ambush requires preparation; running shots lose stationary and trap burst value.
pathfinder.resource_contract: Three Waypoint charges; gain one after moving at least two units between two eligible attacks, once per three seconds; spend one for an enhanced follow-up; ordinary movement alone grants none.

wildguard.loop: Enter the tank form, generate Resolve through real defensive work and spend it before large incoming hits.
wildguard.route_a: Anchored bear: strong self-defense and controlled area threat while holding position.
wildguard.route_b: Mobile guardian: use defensive movement and ally coverage with reduced stationary mitigation.
wildguard.tradeoff: Anchoring is less flexible; mobile coverage gives up some personal defense. Humanoid utility does not preserve full tank mitigation.
wildguard.resource_contract: 100 Resolve; eligible mitigated enemy hit +10, maximum once per second; defensive spend 30; active tank form required; no resource from zero-damage friendly effects.

feral.loop: Build Combo Points through claw attacks and decide between immediate finishing damage and maintained bleeds.
feral.route_a: Bleeding pursuit: maintain bleeds while moving between positional opportunities.
feral.route_b: Focused predation: spend more points in short direct windows against one target.
feral.tradeoff: Bleeds are slower on fragile enemies; direct windows require uptime and careful resource pooling.
feral.resource_contract: Energy plus five owner Combo Points; Raking Claw +1; Savage Finish consumes 1–5; form changes preserve no additional duplicate resource pool.

grovekeeper.loop: Apply growing healing seeds, decide when to consume a mature seed and position recovery areas before group damage.
grovekeeper.route_a: Sustained garden: maintain several HoTs and let them mature naturally.
grovekeeper.route_b: Reactive bloom: consume prepared seeds for immediate recovery, then spend time and mana replanting.
grovekeeper.tradeoff: Sustained healing is slower to rescue; consuming seeds trades future healing for current health.
grovekeeper.resource_contract: Three growth stages per seed at 0/4/8 seconds; one seed per caster/target; consuming removes that seed and its remaining healing budget; no duplicate tick at consumption.

starcaller.loop: Alternate solar and lunar spells to control a Cycle state, then release the appropriate spender.
starcaller.route_a: Alternating balance: use both spell families to maintain access to repeated balanced finishes.
starcaller.route_b: Committed phase: stay in one phase longer for stronger short output before an explicit recovery phase.
starcaller.tradeoff: Balance loses maximum phase burst; commitment is more vulnerable to target loss and forced movement.
starcaller.resource_contract: Cycle meter −3 to +3; solar adds one, lunar subtracts one; eligible finisher consumes three units toward zero; no benefit from toggling a phase without a successful action.

stormcaller.loop: Alternate elemental attacks and release Stormcharge through a line, field or priority-target strike.
stormcaller.route_a: Focused discharge: pool for a high-value target with limited chaining.
stormcaller.route_b: Distributed storm: spend through fields and capped chains against groups.
stormcaller.tradeoff: Focus loses area output; field damage requires enemies to remain inside the area.
stormcaller.resource_contract: 100 Stormcharge; alternating eligible elements +15, repeated element +5; spender 30; major discharge 60; one gain per root action, not per target.

spiritmender.loop: Create temporary links with direct heals and choose a limited path for later recovery.
spiritmender.route_a: Close kinship: heal a compact group through efficient short chain jumps.
spiritmender.route_b: Focused memory: spend links on protection and direct recovery of threatened recipients.
spiritmender.tradeoff: Chains lose value when allies spread; focused protection reduces group throughput.
spiritmender.resource_contract: Maximum four linked allies per caster; a link lasts ten seconds; chain jumps within three units, maximum four targets; no target visited twice in one chain.

totemist.loop: Allocate four static-object capacity units and define at most three links; placement and timing determine damage and support.
totemist.route_a: Anchored constellation: retain a stable layout for sustained area effects.
totemist.route_b: Portable pattern: relocate a smaller layout more often with lower peak output.
totemist.tradeoff: Anchoring loses value against movement; portability sacrifices stationary uptime and throughput.
totemist.resource_contract: Four total combat totems including shared-class totems; at most three explicit links; placement cost 4% mana; relocation follows its own cooldown and cannot duplicate old objects.

ironbody.loop: Use a defensive stance to delay a bounded part of damage, then spend Balance to reduce the debt; delayed damage is still owed.
ironbody.route_a: Debt management: prepare mitigation and clear part of the ledger before a dangerous overlap.
ironbody.route_b: Reactive countering: earn Balance through timed defense and accept a smaller delayed-damage pool.
ironbody.tradeoff: A large ledger risks delayed death; reactive defense is less reliable when timing fails.
ironbody.resource_contract: 100 Balance; successful defense +10 once per second; 30 Balance clears 25% of current ledger; delay at most 30% of eligible post-absorb damage over six seconds; no re-delaying debt ticks.

windfist.loop: Alternate distinct martial actions to preserve Flow while generating and spending Chi.
windfist.route_a: Sustained combinations: preserve varied chains and distribute spending.
windfist.route_b: Burst sequences: build a short complete sequence and spend heavily on a bounded finisher.
windfist.tradeoff: Sustained sequences lose peak burst; burst is punished by interruption and target loss.
windfist.resource_contract: Five Chi; generator +1; finisher cost three; Flow is the last three distinct action families with a six-second window, not a second full energy bar.

lifewalker.loop: Use direct recovery and close-range techniques to build Living Chi; choose whether entering melee is safe.
lifewalker.route_a: Martial healing: gain extra Chi from safe attacks while an ally needs recovery.
lifewalker.route_b: Protective meditation: heal at short range and preserve a stationary channel for predictable damage.
lifewalker.tradeoff: Martial healing risks melee exposure; meditation loses damage contribution and mobility.
lifewalker.resource_contract: Five Living Chi; effective primary heal +1; eligible martial action +1 only if an ally is injured; major heal costs three; Mana is the sustained resource.

demonologist.loop: Direct one major demon and build Authority through combined actions rather than unattended pet damage.
demonologist.route_a: Coordinated offense: plan owner/demon attacks and spend Authority in synchronized windows.
demonologist.route_b: Protective contract: use the same command budget for capped interception and wards.
demonologist.tradeoff: Offense sacrifices protection; protection reduces damage. Losing the demon disrupts both but does not remove the owner's basic spell.
demonologist.resource_contract: 100 Authority; owner and demon hit within two seconds grants 10, once per two seconds; combined attack spends 30; one four-capacity demon replaces the lesser summon.

hellcaller.loop: Build Infernal Debt through attacks, then discharge it while managing a capped nonlethal personal cost.
hellcaller.route_a: Controlled furnace: maintain a limited field and repay Debt frequently.
hellcaller.route_b: Risked discharge: pool Debt for a larger attack with explicit health/defense exposure.
hellcaller.tradeoff: Controlled repayment loses peak burst; larger debt risks death from enemy pressure even though the self-cost itself is nonlethal.
hellcaller.resource_contract: 100 Debt; ordinary generator +10 once per action; discharge spends 30 or 60; self-payment capped at 10% maximum health and cannot take the caster below 35% maximum health.

pactbinder.loop: Maintain one contract clause; create progress through paid, successful actions and decide when to settle it.
pactbinder.route_a: Personal contract: spend more of the contract budget on individual damage.
pactbinder.route_b: Shared liability: fund capped allied protection and debuffs at a personal-output cost.
pactbinder.tradeoff: Personal output loses support; allied value depends on recipients acting and taking relevant damage.
pactbinder.resource_contract: One active clause, five progress; paid eligible action adds one, at most once per second; settlement consumes all; changing clause clears progress; self-damage alone cannot generate more progress.
